subject: physics
title: Conservation of Energy
summary: Energy is never created or destroyed — it only changes form. The total energy of a closed system stays constant while it trades between kinetic, potential, heat, light, and sound. In this model a roller coaster runs a loop and a running bar shows the stored height energy draining into motion as the cart rides, then re-storing climb after climb.

plainLanguageExplanation: Here's a law that never breaks: energy can't be created or destroyed — it can only change form. The total amount in a closed system is fixed, forever. In this roller-coaster model you'll watch that: a bar tracks the rider from the top of the hill down into a loop. At the crest guys near the peak, almost all energy is stored (potential); halfway down, it splits into movement (kinetic); rub against the track and a little slips into heat — but the total of height, speed, heat, and sound never changes. What you spend popping a jack-in-the-box early isn't gone; it's in the sound and the stretch. The car brakes to a stop on the model and the bar shows warmth from the brakes — energy turned into heat instead of motion, but never into nothing. Learn this one law and whole fields of physics become a budget book: every joule goes somewhere, and it's simply a matter of tracking which form.

keyFacts.label: The law

keyFacts.label: Closed systems
keyFacts.value: No escape: total energy stays constant

keyFacts.label: Forms it takes
keyFacts.value: Kinetic, potential, thermal, light, sound, chemical

keyFacts.label: The 'loss' trick
keyFacts.value: Heat and sound aren't losses — they're energy in a less usable form

keyFacts.label: Track it
keyFacts.value: At any moment: PE + KE + heat = the same total

whyItMatters: Conservation of energy is the thesis of physics — the first law of thermodynamics. It's how we trace a car's braking, a light bulb's glow and a battery's drain, and it frames every energy question: where did it go? Not questions like 'run out' only mean one form is spent; the energy still exists — so we question sinks, impact craters, and the sun's fusion all through this single law.
tagline: Energy never vanishes, only changes form
didYouKnow: If you bounce a ball to 70% of its drop height, its lost height is not destroyed — it became sound and heat from the floor plus air drag. The zoom that 'disappears' into brakes on every cart of this coaster is still there; it's just heat that spreads through the rails in the rails.

compareReason: Conservation says the total is fixed; efficiency says how much of that total actually did the useful job — the two laws that frame every energy story.
